---
title: "Choose a method"
description: "From the research question to the analysis method a plan stores, in 4 charts."
---

[Documentation](../../docs.html) / [Methods](../../docs.html#methods)

Start from what the research question asks: a difference, a relationship, a prediction or a measurement. Each chart then asks about the kind of answer and the design, and ends at a test. Under each test is the `method` a plan block stores, as SurveyStudio's Plan dialog and `sframe_plan()` write it.

**Roughly normal, no extreme outliers?** This is the check a t test, ANOVA or Pearson correlation relies on. The scores (for paired data, the differences between them) should be close to a bell shape, with no extreme values pulling the mean. With about 30 or more per group, mild skew does no harm. `sframe_assumption_results()` runs the check: Shapiro-Wilk, skewness and kurtosis, and Levene and Brown-Forsythe tests for equal spread. Unequal spread alone does not send you to a rank test, since the independent t test then uses Welch's version. A No, or ordinal answers such as a single Likert item, lead to the rank tests.

## Difference between groups or occasions

From a test for 2 groups or 2 occasions, a 3rd group or occasion leads to the test below it. See [Compare groups](group-comparisons.html), [Compare the same people over time](repeated-measures.html) and [Test an association between categories](associations.html).

<p><img src="../../../docs/methods/choose-difference.svg" alt="Flowchart: scale scores that are roughly normal go to the paired or independent t test, then repeated-measures, one-way or two-way ANOVA or ANCOVA; ordinal answers go to the Wilcoxon signed-rank or Mann-Whitney U test, then Friedman or Kruskal-Wallis; categories go to McNemar or chi-squared, then Cochran&#x27;s Q or Fisher&#x27;s exact test." style="max-width:100%;height:auto"></p>

## Relationship between variables

Two categorical variables go to the same chi-squared test as a difference between groups, reported with Cramer's V or phi. See [Measure how answers go together](correlations.html).

<p><img src="../../../docs/methods/choose-relationship.svg" alt="Flowchart: scale scores that are linear and roughly normal go to Pearson correlation, then partial correlation; ordinal answers go to Spearman, then Kendall&#x27;s tau; categories go to chi-squared, then Fisher&#x27;s exact test." style="max-width:100%;height:auto"></p>

## Predict an outcome

The type of the outcome picks the model. A 3rd variable that changes the strength of an effect is moderation; one that carries it is mediation. See [Predict an outcome](regression.html).

<p><img src="../../../docs/methods/choose-prediction.svg" alt="Flowchart: a scale outcome goes to linear regression, a yes or no outcome to binary or Firth logistic regression, ordered categories to ordinal logistic, unordered choices to multinomial logistic, and a 3rd variable to moderation or mediation." style="max-width:100%;height:auto"></p>

## Measure a construct

Check readiness before an exploratory factor analysis. CFA, CB-SEM and PLS-SEM are written as model syntax, ready to fit in lavaan or seminr. See [Score a scale and check its reliability](scales-reliability.html) and [Check structure and write model syntax](factor-models.html).

<p><img src="../../../docs/methods/choose-measurement.svg" alt="Flowchart: reliability goes to Cronbach&#x27;s alpha and McDonald&#x27;s omega, an unknown structure to the KMO and Bartlett readiness check then exploratory factor analysis, and a specified structure to CFA, CB-SEM or PLS-SEM syntax." style="max-width:100%;height:auto"></p>

## Effect sizes

Each test reports its effect size, with a confidence interval where the method gives one: Cohen's d for t tests, r for the rank tests, eta or omega squared for ANOVA, Cramer's V or phi for chi-squared, and odds ratios for logistic regression.
